The three domains share one fold and family because the family is defined by the shared repeat architecture of the TAL effector DNA-binding module, not by overall sequence length. TAL effectors (from Xanthomonas) have an N-terminal region, a central DNA-binding array of tandem repeats, and a C-terminal region with nuclear localization and activation elements. Each repeat is about 33-35 residues (usually 34) and folds as a helix-loop-helix unit. The units stack into a right-handed superhelical solenoid, which is all-alpha (SCOPe class a). The SCCS code a.298.1.1 reads as fold a.298, superfamily a.298.1, family a.298.1.1. Because the array is built from copies of one repeat unit, a domain covering 1.5 repeats and one covering 30 or more repeats fall in the same family. Their lengths mainly reflect how many repeat copies the crystal or NMR construct and the SCOPe domain boundary include, not a different evolutionary origin or a different fold.

Limits: (1) Family-level homology here rests on the repeat unit, which is a repetitive, modular element. Shared repeat-level similarity supports common ancestry of the module, but it does not mean each domain is a full-length, equivalent homolog, and the terminal non-repeat regions are not necessarily conserved. (2) Membership in a.298.1.1 does not transfer DNA-target specificity. The repeat-variable diresidues (RVDs, at repeat positions 12 and 13) determine base preference, and their mapping to nucleotides is a separate, context-dependent property that must be checked experimentally for each specific array. (3) Do not use one domain as a template for modeling another of very different length without accounting for repeat count, curvature, and the terminal regions. (4) I did not check the SCOPe release files, PDB entry metadata, or the exact boundaries and repeat counts of d2kq5a_, d3v6pa_, and d4cj9a_. Confirming the length and repeat-number differences for these three specific domains requires the release domain definitions and the corresponding PDB entries, and this answer does not verify them.
